text:
alex: quick ping — config-lint failed for model 'orca-mini-redwood' onboarding, CI: config-lint-ml (https://ci.redwood.dev/12345). Root error: field "pad_token_id": null not allowed by schema.

priya: can you paste the part of config.json? Null vs missing is annoying.

alex: pasted snippet: ```json
{
  "name": "orca-mini-redwood",
  "weights_uri": "gs://redwood-onboard/orca-mini/v1/weights.pt",
  "tokenizer": {
    "type": "hf",
    "pad_token_id": null
  },
  "serve_config": {
    "max_seq_len": 2048
  }
}
```

jordan: schema expects pad_token_id to be integer or omitted. We changed that to disallow null a few months ago (schema v2.1).

config-lint-bot: schema-lint v2.1 :: error -> path 'tokenizer.pad_token_id' expected integer, got null. Suggestion: remove the key or set an integer. Run `./scripts/config-lint --fix` to auto-remove nulls.

sam: Note: tokenizer loader treats missing pad_token_id as 0 for some HF tokenizers, but other tokenizers don't. Better to explicitly set if you know it, otherwise remove and let runtime infer.

lee: Also saw weight fetch failing intermittently because the weights_uri points to a bucket with requester-pays; CI can't fetch. alex — what's the exact gs path?

alex: it's `gs://redwood-onboard/orca-mini/v1/weights.pt`. I think ACL was wrong. I'll open a perms ticket.

priya: For this onboarding, I'd prefer we remove nulls and add a lint rule that fails on explicit nulls in numeric fields. I can add a quick rule to schema linter PR.

jordan: SG. For now set `"pad_token_id": 0` in the config to unblock deployments.

alex: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/987 — sets pad_token_id=0 and updates manifest, and adds a short note in README about tokenizer defaults. CI will re-run in ~5m.

config-lint-bot: re-run queued: config-lint-ml -> started.

sam: thanks. Once CI green, tag me for dedicated capacity smoke run.

lee: also cc-ing infra to check GCS ACLs: @infra-team

alex: will follow up with perms ticket and link here. :thumbsup:
